mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within two months signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consistent decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations diminish.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% over three months signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in the same month, it signals a tight labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over three months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it indicates broader economic weakness.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between HOUST declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1%) suggests accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as liquidity is abundant.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances with FEDFUNDS < 1% despite the positive signal, or the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
